reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's Forethought, Readywit, and Fatalist; the frame is stated correctly: the plover wife Constance tells it to Sprawl, inside Victor's tale to Lively.
Fish are narrated in the neuter with Kannada meaning-names; Fatalist's verse becomes one plain sentence that it speaks itself. A merge of Ryder's passers-by into the fishermen is now disclosed.
Age band 12+: a foolish but innocent character dies. Fatalist's clubbing is one calm sentence with Ryder's repeated pounding softened and disclosed; the content note says plainly what happens.
The pause question comes before the net falls; no em dashes; a vocabulary meaning was made more precise after review.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536, under 650 KB; seams measured at x=512 and y=512/1024; no text. One generation, no edits.

The three fish stay distinct in all panels: slim silver-blue Forethought, orange-gold Readywit and stout grey-green Fatalist; the fishermen and boys wear wide shoulder cloths, not cords, with no caste markers.
Panel 4 shows the net with two fish inside but no harm; panel 5 Readywit leaping from the bank; Fatalist's death is not drawn and panel 6 is a calm sunset with Readywit safe in the reeds.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children or parents.
Source fidelity was checked against saved copies of the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.

Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol (gpt-6.1-sol is not available to this account) and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels, not in the app in dark mode.
